title: C¹ Approximation Theorem for Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0 and let f : ℝ^n → ℝ be K-Lipschitz. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a C¹ function g : ℝ^n → ℝ with L^n({x : f(x) ≠ g(x)} ∪ {x : Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε. Here ℝ^n = Euclid n, L^n is Lebesgue measure on it (volume), and Df(x) is the Fréchet derivative (Lean fderiv ℝ f x, which is 0 where f is not differentiable).
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε
